chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Dawood ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) while I had with me three letters without addresses, and they had become confused to me, so I became distressed. He took one of them and said: “This is the letter of Ziyad ibn Shabib.” Then he took the second and said: “This is the letter of so-and-so.” I was astonished, and he looked at me and smiled.

He said: He gave me three hundred dinars and instructed me to carry them to one of the sons of his uncle, and he said: “Indeed, he will say to you: ‘Direct me to a trader who can buy goods for me with it,’ so direct him to one.” He said: So I went to him with the dinars, and he said to me: “O Abu Hashim, direct me to a trader who can buy goods for me with it.” So I said: “Yes.”

He said: A camel-driver asked me to speak to him on his behalf so that he might include him in some of his affairs. So I entered upon him to speak to him for him, and I found him eating with a group, and I was unable to speak to him. So he said: “O Abu Hashim, eat.” And he placed food before me. Then he said, initiating it himself without being asked: “O boy, see to the camel-driver whom Abu Hashim brought to us, and attach him to yourself.”

He said: One day I entered an orchard with him, and I said to him: “May I be made your ransom, I am strongly attached to eating clay, so supplicate to Allah for me.” He remained silent. Then after three days, initiating it himself, he said to me: “O Abu Hashim, Allah has removed from you the eating of clay.” Abu Hashim said: There is nothing more hateful to me than it today.

key_terms.ابْتِدَاءً: initiating the matter without being asked
key_terms.الطِّينِ: clay, which Abu Hashim had a strong habit of eating
key_terms.جَمَّالٌ: a camel-driver seeking inclusion in the Imam's affairs
key_terms.حَرِيفٍ: a trader or merchant engaged to purchase goods
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin used here as financial support
key_terms.رِقَاعٍ: letters or written slips carried by the narrator
key_terms.فَادْعُ اللَّهَ: supplicate to Allah on my behalf

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the knowledge, concern, and answered du'a of Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration recounts several signs of the knowledge and care of Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام): identifying letters without marks, foretelling a relative's exact request, and responding to an unspoken need regarding a camel-driver. It also relates his du'a for Abu Hashim, after which Allah removed his attachment to eating clay.
